Maasdam.label: grow eyes

facts.v: Cow's milk, often centrifuged to remove spores (spore-sensitive type)

Maasdam.text: Maasdam is a washed-curd Dutch cheese to which propionic acid bacteria are added; during a warm-room stage they multiply and ferment lactate to CO2, propionate and acetate, giving large round eyes and a sweet, nutty taste. Its low salt, high moisture and warm ripening make it prone to butyric spoilage, so the milk is often centrifuged to remove spores.

The larvae break down the paste, which turns soft to spreadably creamy with a strong, penetrating, piquant taste.

plantCheese.text: Instead of calf rennet or acid, a plant enzyme clots the milk. Which plant decides the cheese: cardoon in Iberian ewe's-milk cheeses, Calotropis in West African wagashi, papaya in Indonesian dangke. The enzyme of Calotropis procera sets the milk but breaks protein down little, so the cheese can be reboiled every other day and kept for about a month (Licitra, quoted in Seini et al. 2018).
